subject: Day 1: track output, confirm screens, call pediatrician
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 1. Output is the primary objective: at least one wet diaper per day-of-life until day 5 (so two by end of today), and the first stool — meconium, black and tarry — should already have passed. Feeds and color trajectory dominate the rest of the agenda. Avi is on his way through the metabolic-stabilization week.

Action items
- If you have not yet called your chosen pediatrician for the first-week visit, call this morning. Day 3-5 is the target window. AAP HealthyChildren on choosing a pediatrician: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/family-life/health-management/Pages/default.aspx
- Confirm in writing that the metabolic newborn screen and the CCHD pulse-oximetry screen passed before discharge. These are state-mandated; the hospital will give you a printout or send results to the pediatrician portal. CDC overview of newborn screening: https://www.cdc.gov/newborn-screening/about/index.html
- Submit the birth certificate paperwork if it was not filed at the hospital. SSA application page for Avi's Social Security card: https://www.ssa.gov/ssnumber/. You will need the SSN to open the 529 plan and claim him as a dependent.
- Latch checks every feed if breastfeeding. Asymmetric latch with the nipple deep, lips flanged outward, audible swallows. If pain is sharp or wounds form within 24 hours, schedule a lactation consult before discharge if possible. Find an IBCLC: https://ilca.org/
- Begin a feeding log: time, side or volume, duration, wet/dirty count. The pediatrician will ask at the day 3-5 visit.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Newborn rash (erythema toxicum), milia, peeling skin, occasional sneezes. Single black meconium stool passed.
- [low concern] Faint yellow tinge limited to the face after day 1; physiologic jaundice peaks around day 3-5.
- [monitor] Fewer wet diapers than days-of-life by the morning of day 2 (i.e., zero by tonight). Re-check latch and feeding cadence.
- [call within 24h] Yellow tinge extending below the chest. Inability to latch despite multiple attempts. Persistent sleepiness through more than one feeding window.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). In infants under 90 days this is a workup-required event, full stop. Lethargy that does not respond to stimulation, refusal of all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. AAP HealthyChildren on fever in newborns: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx

Enrichment opportunity
Skin-to-skin contact stays the default holding mode this week. It regulates Avi's temperature, glucose, and breathing while supporting milk supply. CDC on breastfeeding and skin-to-skin: https://www.cdc.gov/breastfeeding/index.html

Upcoming
- Day 3-5: first-week pediatrician visit (target window).
- Day 7-10: weight check; most term infants regain birth weight by day 14.
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt.

Further reading
- The Happiest Baby on the Block by Harvey Karp — the 5 S's for soothing a newborn: https://www.happiestbaby.com/pages/dr-harvey-karp
- Cribsheet by Emily Oster — evidence-based decisions from birth to preschool: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/562146/cribsheet-by-emily-oster/
- AAP HealthyChildren overview of the first month: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- CDC overview of breastfeeding fundamentals: https://www.cdc.gov/breastfeeding/index.html
